answer: Resist sybils with randomly assigned useful-work quotas: each identity must complete a fresh, verifier-assigned computation, proving a dataset chunk or indexing new records, before its weight counts. A mesa of standing is built only from checked results, not from names: proofs are bound to the identity key, so one result cannot serve two agents. An attacker planting ten thousand fakes in the orchard must run ten thousand separate jobs, each costing real compute and time, with shale-hard verification rejecting copied or reused proofs, while an honest agent does one job and keeps its standing.
